## Highlights

- Project agents run each task in a separate worker. A busy agent can take another
  eligible task without another agent definition; organization and host capacity
  still limit concurrent work. Agent workspaces survive sandbox replacement, and
  active turns can recover from a temporary spawner restart.
  [#4603](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4603),
  [#4560](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4560),
  [#4585](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4585)
- Managed schedules can wake a project's standing coordinator when an agent frees
  its slot. Concurrent completions coalesce into one pending wake, with normal
  admission checks and retry backoff. This reduces the wait for the next scheduled
  dispatch without bypassing provider or host limits.
  [#4608](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4608)
- Operational review contexts can handle a declared batch of up to twenty captured
  reviews. Each target still needs its independent review decision and matching
  evidence. A review context does not create another review of its own report;
  requesting changes completes the review action while leaving the implementation
  unfinished.
  [#4616](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4616)
- Coding agents can read and edit automation versions through MCP with version
  conflict checks, retained settings, project installation controls, saved-version
  tests and deployment history. Definition changes record their source and client
  in the audit trail. Discovery tools, resources and prompts help clients find
  available models, skills and automation inputs.
  [#4592](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4592)
- Usage limits now cover transcriptions, knowledge embeddings, chat titles and
  later model rounds. Indexing that reaches a usage limit can wait and resume.
  Subscription-backed managed agent turns count as requests at no model cost;
  connector calls are counted separately from model requests. Agent runs started
  with an API key also count toward that key.
  [#4525](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4525),
  [#4541](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4541),
  [#4520](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4520),
  [#4555](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4555),
  [#4550](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4550),
  [#4558](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4558)
- Sandbox maintenance reduces repeated Docker and BuildKit work and adds a critical
  disk-pressure tier for reclaiming released idle sessions. Busy sessions use
  graceful shutdown, and Kubernetes placement and startup checks retain resource
  bounds.
  [#4604](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4604),
  [#4602](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4602),
  [#4597](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4597)
- Private deployment acceptance can use a captured gateway container while keeping
  the canonical HTTPS hostname, certificate validation and serving-process checks.
  Its receipt records the gateway and network used.
  [#4617](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4617)
- Maintainers can retire obsolete merge-group validation runs with source and queue
  checks. A separate finishing mode handles only an exact reviewed workflow whose
  real jobs have ended and whose remaining summary jobs are unallocated. Requests
  and uncertain outcomes are retained; cancellation never counts as passing CI.
  [#4613](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4613)

## Upgrade notes

- Use this release's reviewed CLI and matching runtime images. Back up the
  application and knowledge databases, configuration, keys and external stores.
  When upgrading from v0.5.77 or earlier, also follow the inherited
  [v0.5.79 upgrade requirements](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/blob/0ee5fd9656dc12f08976155d956ee76fe39f4ea3/.github/release-notes/v0.5.79.md#upgrade-notes):
  the supported legacy runtime bridge, zero unfinished automation census, managed
  protocol-2 cutover, vector-copy disk headroom and forward-repair restrictions
  still apply. Those retained notes are source history, not proof of a completed
  deployment. Do not clear execution holds or retag earlier versions.
- Apply the complete ordered application migration inventory. This release adds
  direct-call holds, chat project stamps, agent-run key attribution, knowledge
  author attribution, agent handles and worker records, pending project wakes,
  operational review contexts, MCP activity and automation version attribution.
  Existing migration filenames remain immutable, including the two distinct
  `0164` files. The new runtime and its CLI must agree on the installed database
  floor; do not roll back by manually starting an older image.
- Enable early coordinator wakes explicitly with `wakeOnSlotFreed: true` in the
  schedule's managed configuration and apply it through the Tale CLI. Only one
  schedule may claim a project's wake, and existing schedules retain their current
  behavior until configured. Enroll a pristine operational task before using review
  batches; an implementation task with retained work cannot be repurposed as a
  review context. Neither feature grants credentials or guarantees a particular
  number of concurrent workers.
- Update integrations for REST/OpenAPI contract `3.27.0` and the published MCP
  schemas. MCP argument validation now returns structured tool errors, and reads
  offer structured content. Clients using the newer protocol revision must send
  its matching request metadata and headers; earlier supported protocol revisions
  remain available. Automations installed only in projects the caller cannot read
  are hidden on both MCP and REST reads.
- Review request and token caps for subscription-backed agents, and allow for the
  newly counted transcription and embedding work. Earlier usage is not backfilled,
  and older processes do not write every new usage dimension during a mixed-version
  rollout. Finish retiring those processes before relying on uniform accounting.
  See [Policies and limits](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/admin/governance/policies-and-limits).
- A deployment adapter using `--origin-container` must supply the full running
  gateway ID and consume the optional `serving.originRoute` receipt. A gateway
  restart, identity change or ambiguous network makes acceptance fail. This proves
  the captured private route; it does not prove public DNS or off-host reachability.
  Keep ordinary monitoring for those paths.
